A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CHAMP and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Human3.6M and MPI-INF-3DHP experiments, ablations, empirical coverage measurements, and qualitative pose predictions.

after.justification: V2 reports the retained benchmark experiments and additional score-error analysis, single-frame evaluation, robustness cases, and quantitative 3DPW transfer results.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 replace the pairwise cosine-similarity conformity score with a conditional discriminator producing a scalar score. V2 introduces discriminator-training and adversarial denoiser losses, combines adversarial and set-size losses, and replaces inference scoring against a 20-pose mean reference with direct scoring and score-weighted aggregation.

E1.justification: V2 adds image-only pose estimation, distinct from v1's single-hypothesis evaluation using video sequences, and explicit truncation, incorrect-keypoint, and self-occlusion scenarios. Appendix L adds MPII training coverage and quantitative transfer evaluation on 3DPW, which v1 only mentioned as a qualitative video source.

E2.justification: V2 adds CHAMP-Naive-Agg to Tables 1–2, enabling comparison against J-Agg without CP filtering. New comparisons include 3DMB, HuMOR, POCO, RoHM, and KNOWN in Table 3, and CameraPose in Table 6. Table 1's D3DP-Agg-to-D3DP relabeling retains the same baseline scores.

E3.justification: The stated loss weight changes from 0.05 to 0.6, and Figures 5–6 revise the hypothesis-count and loss-weight sweeps. New protocols include N=1 training, a 500-sample score-error study, and transfer testing with ground-truth 2D inputs after joint Human3.6M/MPII training. The original actor splits and 2% calibration holdout remain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained scoring-function, hypothesis-count, loss-weight, and coverage studies, v2 adds score-error correlation analysis and a control separating CP filtering from J-Agg. Appendices I–K add failure visualizations, a test of dependence on temporal context, and qualitative investigations of truncation, incorrect keypoints, and self-occlusion.

E5.justification: Section 5.4 newly applies Pearson correlation and ordinary least-squares regression to 500 test samples, reporting correlation and R-squared statistics. Neither version provides repeated-run variability, seed counts, or confidence intervals; the empirical coverage reporting practice remains.

E6.justification: Many CHAMP results are replaced: reported CHAMP-Agg Human3.6M MPJPE changes from 36.0 to 34.8 mm, and P-MPJPE from 30.2 to 27.9 mm. These accompany the revised method and loss weight. V2 also adds uncertainty-method comparisons, single-frame results, 3DPW results, and score-error and failure findings; Tables 5–6 report CHAMP-Agg at 37.1 mm MPJPE and 60.8 mm PA-MPJPE respectively.

T1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 substantively revise the mathematical score and prediction-set definitions, introduce discriminator/adversarial objectives, and change the corresponding coverage indicator in Appendix A. The DDIM derivation and exchangeability premise remain, and neither version supplies a new proof establishing CHAMP-specific coverage.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: sequence-to-sequence multi-hypothesis pose estimation, learned conformal filtering, improved aggregation, state-of-the-art performance, and inherited CP guarantees. The revised method and additional evidence do not materially redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations connecting conformity scores, prediction error, input ambiguity, and hypothesis diversity, including failure when most hypotheses are inaccurate and dependence on the 2D detector. Section 6 adds slow scoring-model training and lack of shape estimation, while dropping its explicit warning that theoretical coverage cannot be fully justified; exchangeability concerns remain in Section 5.5 and Appendix A.

D1.justification: V2 updates the documented loss weight, changes reported GPU memory consumption from 18 GB to 30 GB, and revises the scoring MLP's output description. It adds a project-site link for visualization and promised code/data, plus a reproducibility statement. The PDFs do not establish that the promised resources were released.

R1.justification: Section 5.4 and new Appendix F substantially expand positioning against uncertainty-aware human pose and shape reconstruction, distinguishing CHAMP from POCO, HuMOR, RoHM, KNOWN, and 3DMB. V2 also adds adversarial-learning references and replaces numerous Section 2 citations, including several robotics/manipulation works with human-pose literature.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted rewrites to scoring, inference, and limitations, adds ethics and reproducibility statements, and inserts additional appendix sections. The introduction, principal section order, and much of the existing explanatory text remain closely matched; this is not a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 adds the correlation plot, score-colored and failure visualizations, robustness panels, and three comparison tables. It expands Tables 1–2 with a control row and redraws ablation plots with revised axes. Earlier qualitative figures are retained but relocated or resized, alongside the conference-format layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation: the added CHAMP-Naive-Agg control better isolates filtering's contribution, while single-frame and held-out 3DPW tests and explicit failure cases examine applicability beyond v1's principal video benchmarks. These address important gaps in attribution and failure analysis. Tradeoffs remain: the coverage warning is less explicit in Section 6, and the new correlation of -0.41 and OLS R-squared of 0.26 require reconciliation. These weaknesses limit individual claims but do not outweigh the substantial gain in diagnostic evidence.
